feature: Math.compact(n: number): string is a bespoke (invented) built-in added under the Math namespace, so the static type checker treats it as `any` and no TypeSystem change is needed. It is implemented as a 3-helper pipeline: Compact (sign + unit dispatch) -> CompactScaled (unit select, round, carry) -> FormatOneDecimal / RoundHalfUpOneDecimal (rendering).
contract: 2. If abs(n) < 1000: return floor(abs) as a plain integer string, no decimals (42 -> '42', 999 -> '999', 750 -> '750').
3. 1000 <= abs < 1e6: value = abs/1000 rounded HALF-UP (ties away from zero) to 1 decimal, suffix 'K'; a trailing '.0' is dropped (1000 -> '1K', 1500 -> '1.5K', 1450 -> '1.5K', 1234 -> '1.2K').
4. 1e6 <= abs < 1e9: same with /1e6 and suffix 'M'; abs >= 1e9: /1e9 and suffix 'B'.
5. CARRY rule: if rounding to 1 decimal lifts the scaled value to 1000.0 of its unit, carry to the next unit (999950 -> '1M' not '1000K'; 999950000 -> '1B' not '1000M').

BUG_1_rounding_half_up.effect: Math.Round uses banker's rounding (ties to even) instead of half-up (ties away from zero). On exact .X5 tenth ties the result is one tenth too low: 1.45 -> 1.4 instead of 1.5. Non-tie values and whole values are unaffected, so the symptom only shows on certain decimals (matches the vague 'decimals don't seem right' report).

BUG_2_carry_threshold.effect: The carry test uses strict > 1000.0 instead of >= 1000.0, so a value that rounds to exactly 1000.0 of its unit never carries and is rendered as '1000K' / '1000M' instead of carrying to '1M' / '1B'.

BUG_3_negative_sign_dropped.effect: The negative branch recurses on abs(n) but drops the leading '-', so negative inputs render with no sign: -1500 -> '1.5K', -42 -> '42'.

bug_independence: Each bug breaks a disjoint set of checks. BUG 1 only affects exact .X5 tenth ties (carry cases like 999.95 still round to 1000.0 under both half-up and banker's, so BUG 2 cases are stable under BUG 1 alone). BUG 2 only affects values that round to exactly 1000.0 of a unit. BUG 3 only affects negative inputs. No check exercises more than one bug.
partial_fix_traps: The prompt hints ONLY at the rounding/decimals symptom (BUG 1). Fixing only BUG 1 makes c1-c4 pass but leaves BUG 2 (c5, c6, c7) and BUG 3 (c8, c9) failing -> 7/12 = 0.583, below the 0.9 gate.
Fixing BUG 1 + BUG 2 but not BUG 3 -> c8/c9 still fail -> 10/12 = 0.833, below gate.
Fixing BUG 1 + BUG 3 but not BUG 2 -> c5/c6/c7 still fail -> 9/12 = 0.75, below gate.
A solver who treats this as a single rounding fix matching the vague report cannot pass; the gate forces reading the helpers and discovering the carry-threshold and negative-sign bugs.
